tip: Position words like arkasında (behind) put the noun in the genitive: caminin arkasında means at the back of the mosque.
For reported speech the verb takes -eceğini: geleceğini means that she would come, followed by söyledi (said).
Here yeni means just or recently, not new: yeni yürümeyi öğrendi means has just learned to walk.
The suffix -ince means when or once something happens: esince means when it blew.
Passive uses edildi (was done) with a noun: inşa edildi means was built, and no doer is named.
Add -ki to make a possessive pronoun: seninki means yours, and seninkini adds the object ending -ni.
The suffix -ken means while: yağarken means while it was raining, marking two things happening at once.
Comparisons use ablative -den plus daha: ötekinden daha ilginç means more interesting than the other one.
For after doing something use -tikten sonra: yaptıktan sonra means after doing it.
To name the doer in a passive, use tarafından (by): binlerce kişi tarafından means by thousands of people.
The suffix -yla means with: başarısıyla means with her success, one word doing the job of a preposition.
To say despite, use -masına rağmen: yağmasına rağmen means despite the fact that it rained.
Nouns pair with yapmak (to do) to form verbs: spor yapıyorum means I do sport, that is I exercise.
